u2fd: Ignore unsupported vendor mode command Existing builds of cr50 support the vendor mode commands, but future builds will not. If we get a NoSuchCommand error, it means we are running against one of these newer builds, which do not have a notion of 'mode', and therefore we do not need to set it. Ignore such errors if we encounter them. tpm_manager: remove stale local data from the disk After TPM ownership is cleared, tpm manager local data becomes stale. If it's somehow not wiped after reboot/encstateful remount, the stale data will show up in TPM status (e.g., the output of `tpm_manager_client status`) and/or be reused by tpm manager again. This change detects and removes stale local data shortly after tpm_managerd starts. BUG=chromium:974313 TEST=Unit tests. On a soraka: 1. Take tpm ownership, define a new NV space, soft-clear tpm, restart tpm_managerd, run tpm_manager_client status, and make sure all the stale data is gone, including the nvram policy. 2. Following 1, define another new NV space, restart tpm_managerd, run tpm_manager_client status again, and make sure a policy of the new space is added. 3. Following 2, take ownership, restart tpm_managerd, and make sure the new local data isn't removed. 4. Manually modify trunks utility to fail after the endorsement password is set, soft-clear tpm, restart tpm_managerd, and take ownership. Make sure take ownership fails but local data contains the new passwords. Then, restart tpm_managerd and make sure nothing is wiped in the local data. On a chell: Do the same tests above by replacing soft-clearing tpm with backing up and restoring stale /var/lib/tpm_manager/local_tpm_data, simulating an unwiped encstateful. Change-Id: I351a82f1843f6e752c7b46433c80c2def4b14535 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1765808 Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com>

vm_tools: concierge: Add API to disable and lock SMT state As part of supporting untrusted VMs, SMT needs to be disabled in certain conditions.
